headline: Net income slips on higher costs despite strong summer heat
summary_short: Pinnacle West's Q2 2026 net income fell 7.3% y/y to $178.6M ($1.43 diluted EPS, -9.5% y/y) as higher interest and depreciation costs outweighed 7.1% y/y revenue growth to $1,455.7M from early, heavy summer cooling demand.
summary_long: Revenue grew 7.1% y/y to $1,455.7M on unusually early and sustained summer heat: residential customer growth of 2.1%, weather-normalized sales growth of 5.6%, and total sales up 9.6%. Operating income was roughly flat (-0.6% y/y) at $305.7M. Net income fell 7.3% y/y to $178.6M ($1.43 diluted EPS, -9.5% y/y) as a roughly $14M combined drag from higher interest charges, higher depreciation and amortization, and lower transmission revenue outweighed favorable weather, customer growth, lower O&M expense, and lower taxes. Cash fell to $9.1M from $18.8M a year ago; long-term debt rose 14.9% y/y to $9,775.8M. Pinnacle West continues to estimate FY2026 weather-normalized diluted EPS of $4.55-$4.75, unchanged from prior guidance.

drivers.explanation: Company attributes the increase to unusually early, sustained summer heat driving cooling demand, with 2.1% residential customer growth and 5.6% weather-normalized sales growth; total sales rose 9.6%.

Release states the ~$14M y/y decline reflects higher interest charges, higher depreciation and amortization, and lower transmission service revenue, partly offset by favorable weather, customer growth, lower O&M expense, and lower taxes.
EPS fell further (-9.5%) than net income (-7.3%) because diluted weighted-average shares outstanding rose 2.2% y/y (124.5M vs 121.9M), adding dilution beyond the earnings decline.
CEO Ted Geisler said results were within expectations despite the y/y decline, citing a 7% y/y increase in residential cooling degree days from unusually early, sustained summer heat.
